newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Cook unveils Euro business strategy.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Cook unveils Euro business strategy.

text.p: Robin Cook, foreign affairs spokesman of Britain's opposition Labour Party, on Tuesday unveiled a six-point business plan for Europe including calls for freer competition, new budget priorities and action against fraud.

Cook, in a speech to businessmen in London, also said Labour would "guarantee that the decisions on the single currency are based on a hard-headed assessment of its economic practicalities, rather than political dogma".
Cook said there could be "no fudging or fiddling the rules" of a single currency and nations wanting to join would have to show genuine convergence in their economies.
"In the case of Britain, the only one judgment which should be applied is whether joining a single currency would be in our own national interest," Cook said.
Aside from the single currency, the other five points of Labour's business plan for Europe addressed the single market, the community budget, enlargement, economic stability and fraud.
Cook said Labour wanted a "level playing field" in energy, telecommunications, bio-technology and financial services.
Labour would also press for new priorities in the community budget, switching spending away from the Common Agricultural Policy into economic sectors which would provide jobs in the next century.

Labour would also press for a "flying start" to negotiations to enlarge the European Union to take in countries in central and eastern Europe. Cook said Labour also wanted a European Recovery Fund which would be built up in periods of growth to be used to invest in infrastructure in recession.
Cook said Labour would demand tough action on governments which turned a blind eye to fraud against Brussels.
